newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean banks agree to cut lending rates.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean banks agree to cut lending rates.

text.p: South Korean banks agreed to lower bank lending rates by about a percentage point in the near future to help companies improve their international competitiveness, the Korea Federation of Banks said on Friday.
At the end of August, South Korea's bank lending rates averaged 11.03 percent and prime rates ranged from 8.75 percent to 9.50 percent, according to the central Bank of Korea.
Heads of the federation's 35 member banks held a meeting on Friday and agreed to join the government's campaign to hone competitiveness, a spokesman for the federation said.
No set timetable was agreed on for cutting rates, he said.
The central bank said last week it would cut the bank reserve requirement ratio to an average of 5.5 percent on November 8 from 7.4 percent at present.
Analysts and bank officials say the cut in the ratio will likely translate into a reduction by about 0.25 of a percentage point in the prime lending rates.
The requirement ratio is the portion of money out of total deposits that banks have to deposit with the central bank.
